common_name: Leafy Coral Blow (Red Rocket Firecracker Plant)

planting.note: Set out container-grown plants or rooted cuttings in spring once soil has warmed, in well-drained soil in full sun to light shade; unlike its wiry-stemmed cousin coral fountain, leafy coral blow forms an upright, leafy shrub rather than a cascading mound, so give it more room to fill out as a mid-size border or hedge component.

directions: Russelia sarmentosa, known as leafy coral blow or red rocket, is a Mexican and Central American native that differs from the familiar coral fountain (Russelia equisetiformis) in carrying full, ovate green leaves along upright-arching stems rather than reduced, rush-like green stems. From summer into fall it produces dense whorled clusters of slender, deep-red to crimson tubular flowers at the stem tips, and the long bloom display draws ruby-throated hummingbirds and butterflies heavily along the Gulf Coast. Plant it in well-drained soil in full sun for the densest flowering, though it tolerates part shade with a looser, more open habit. It is drought-tolerant once established but flowers more generously with regular moisture during the growing season, and in zone 9 it typically dies back to the roots after a hard freeze, resprouting reliably by late spring.
